Beyond the shared-objective R0 regime in Section~\ref{sec:num-real},
R1 partitions the retained data randomly and disjointly; R2 assigns two label-sorted shards to each client. For R1/R2, seed 4101 defines primary partitions and 4102/4103 define separately reported sensitivity partitions. Equal client weights preserve the global empirical objective. IID partitioning does not make finite-sample objectives identical. The R0 aggregate covariance described in Section~\ref{sec:num-real}
has trace $0.001060$ after rounding; R1/R2 reference covariances can change
with their partitions.
new:
In the shared-objective setting, every client uses the same empirical
objective. The disjoint IID setting instead partitions the examples
randomly; the label-skew setting assigns two label-sorted shards to each
client. Both disjoint settings use a fixed primary partition and two
alternative partitions for sensitivity checks. Equal client weights
preserve the global empirical objective, but IID partitioning does not
make finite-sample local objectives identical. The shared-objective
aggregate covariance described in Section~\ref{sec:num-real} has trace
$0.001060$ after rounding; disjoint partitions may have different
reference covariances.

\subsection{Run-length and numerical sensitivity}
\label{app:supp-audit}

First/last-half projected contrasts do not exclude zero under the
$2\times69$ family adjustment, but this is not a test of temporal
equivalence. Four of the 68 algorithm--configuration comparisons in
the independent controlled study have nominal raw-versus-balance
intervals excluding zero; the balance estimator remains primary.
In the shared-objective real-data study, the direct and primary
observables coincide by construction, so their agreement is not a
separate validation.

The first- and last-half endpoint allocation contrasts are $0.003098$
and $0.003129$ for SCAFFOLD, and $0.002053$ and $0.002092$ for FedAvg.
These subdivisions of the same 64 batches support within-tail
consistency, but are not independent or longer-run replications.

The short-run update-identity and affine-translation checks pass.
Over longer trajectories, 48 of 132 $H=1$ arithmetic checks exceed
the strict $10^{-10}$ tolerance, with a maximum vector discrepancy
of about $7.54\times10^{-10}$. The shared-objective subset has 24
exceedances among 60 checks and maximum coordinate discrepancy
$4.33\times10^{-10}$. Two additional shared-objective paths using
a stable endpoint-increment computation reduce vector discrepancies
to about $10^{-12}$. These two checks do not establish numerical
agreement over the full set of configurations and do not replace
the reported results.
